source_evidence: Exact player 'investigate' authorizes examining the lower-gallery obstruction with companions, not disturbing it. D338~06:19–06:24; Cirren's earlier Detect Magic expires naturally at06:20, then he self-casts Guidance and makes Investigation with V's routine feasible Help (V holds light/helps compare tool marks and stone placement, no dangerous commitment). Predetermined DC14 distinguishes deliberately packed dry-stone rubble from natural collapse; DC18 identifies the supported lip and a plausible safe removal approach. Actual visible Python secrets batch411dfcf8f3ce70fe5f5fb6d076f6a51b, advantage d20 faces12,7 keep12+7 Investigation + Guidance d4=4=23, both thresholds met. Physical evidence: smaller stones deliberately wedged between larger stones, repeated fresh tool marks and a roughly level face; loose fall debris was deliberately packed into the descending natural crack, rather than entirely random collapse. Above the packing, a fractured overhanging slab rests on one side of the rock lip; pulling lower stones or the supporting wedge could destabilize it. A faint cool draft passes through a small gap; suggests connected airspace but no verified chamber, depth, exit, occupant, ore value or purpose. Cirren identifies a cautious method: leave load-bearing wedges and existing timber props untouched, first brace the fractured lip and remove loose top stones in a controlled sequence. Existing picks, rope, wedges and local timber props are visible but suitability of additional bracing and actual clearing remain to resolve; no guaranteed safe removal, no digging, no new trap or monster established. Fenar can help with physical work if V authorizes. No unfamiliar magic observed before Detect Magic expiry; Guidance expires on check; Light shield remains until~07:10. No loot transfer, spell slot/limited resource expenditure, damage, consumption or further descent.
